thread.title_full: Trump-Backed Pastor Abruptly Quits Congressional Race After Secret Texts Exposed

author: Jack Whitmore
title: Trump-Backed Pastor Abruptly Quits Congressional Race After Secret Texts Exposed
text:
Trump-backed Tulsa pastor Jackson Lahmeyer has abruptly quit the GOP primary runoff for Oklahoma’s 1st Congressional District.
His exit follows a texting scandal that derailed his campaign just as Trump pulled his endorsement.
Pastor Suspends Campaign Lahmeyer announced his withdrawal in a statement Wednesday.
“After prayerful consideration with my wife, Kendra, and my team over the last twenty four hours, I’ve made the difficult decision to suspend my campaign for Congress,” he said.
“I do not want to be a distraction to my family, my church, and the great people of Oklahoma’s 1st Congressional District,” he continued.
Jackson Lahmeyer
He said the district deserves a strong conservative voice in Washington.
His statement came minutes after Trump rescinded his endorsement.
Texting Scandal Erupts Lahmeyer’s campaign took a hit Sunday after the Daily Mail published intimate text messages.
The exchanges were between Lahmeyer and Caitlin Key, who is not his wife.
In them, he allegedly called her “cute” and invited her to his hotel room.
Key, who was Miss Oklahoma USA 2007, reportedly worked as a fundraiser for his campaign.
She told the Daily Mail the two met in 2022.
The story quickly engulfed the pastor’s bid.
Lahmeyer Responds Lahmeyer acknowledged the reporting in a Facebook post.
He admitted to “crossing a boundary line through text messaging” and said he “ended all communication.”
He argued the messages were “carefully cherry-picked to create an impression that is not accurate.”
Jackson Lahmeyer
He told The Hill his decision to drop out was not because of Trump’s switch.
“I decided to choose my wife over my ambition,” he said.
He said he had made the decision the night before Trump’s announcement.
Trump Switches Support Trump rescinded his endorsement and backed state Rep. Mark Tedford instead.
The move came a day after both candidates advanced to an Aug. 25 runoff.
“I greatly appreciate Jackson Lahmeyer’s hard work under difficult circumstances,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
“But, when it comes to the current Congressional race… I will be supporting America First Patriot, Mark Tedford,” he added.
Mark Tedford
Lahmeyer had been seen as close to the MAGA movement with deep ties to its allies.
He helped mobilize evangelical voters for Trump’s 2024 campaign.
Tedford Now the Favorite Lahmeyer’s exit leaves Tedford as the Republican nominee.
He is now in a strong position to win the general election.
Trump won the Tulsa-anchored district in 2024 by 21 percentage points.
Cook Political Report rates the seat as solid red.
House Speaker Mike Johnson also threw his support behind Tedford.
He said Tedford “will help us continue to deliver safe streets, secure borders, a strong economy, and peace through strength.”
Filling Hern’s Seat Tedford is looking to succeed Rep. Kevin Hern.
Hern won the Republican primary for Oklahoma’s open Senate seat.
That seat opened after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin joined Trump’s Cabinet.
The runoff will now decide the GOP standard-bearer in the deep-red district.
The general election winner will represent the district in Washington.

Lahmeyer’s campaign took a hit Sunday after the Daily Mail published intimate text messages. “I greatly appreciate Jackson Lahmeyer’s hard work under difficult circumstances,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. That seat opened after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin joined Trump’s Cabinet.
